newsitem.title: ITALY: RUGBY UNION-WALES SURVIVE COMEBACK FOR FIRST WIN IN ITALY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WALES SURVIVE COMEBACK FOR FIRST WIN IN ITALY.

text.p: Wales survived a brave second-half comeback from Italy to win their first-ever full international on Italian soil 31-22 at the Olympic stadium on Saturday.

Nine points in arrears at halftime, Italy fought back with a try from Ivan Francescato to lead 22-21 with 15 minutes remaining, but Gareth Thomas's second try of the match and some spirited Welsh defending denied the Italians an historic win.

The home side, a growing force in international rugby, were left to rue a dismal start that saw them 13 points down in as many minutes, and a controversial decision by South African referee Carl Spannenberg.

In the 35th miniute, with Italy 28-22 down, Spannenberg ruled that centre Scott Gibbs beat Andrea Sgorlon in a race for the ball, after the Italian flanker had charged Neil Jenkins' clearance kick over the try line.
But a television replay suggested Sgorlon had got the vital first touch after Gibbs had dived over the ball.
In a fiercely fought match, Welsh full-back Wayne Proctor was carried off at the start of the second half after a mid-air collision with Italian winger Paolo Vaccari.

Out-scored by three tries to one, and over reliant on the place-kicing of their Argentine-born fly-half Diego Dominguez, who got five penalties, defeat was a blow to Italy's hopes of winning a place in the Five Nations tournament.
The Italians were three points down inside two minutes, Jenkins kicking his first penalty from in front of the posts.

Robert Howley should have scored Wales' opening try in the eighth minute after intercepting a pass just inside the Italian half, but with a clear run to the line, the scrum-half slipped and lost the ball one metre short.
From the resulting scrum, full-back Massimo Ravazzolo's weak clearance missed touch, leaving winger Daffyll James with a clear run down the touchline to score in the corner.
Jenkins converted and added a penalty in the 20th minute to leave his side deservedly 13 points up after 13 minutes.
With the Welsh forwards dominant in the rucks and mauls, and Gibbs and Thomas a constant threat in the centre, Italy only ventured out of their own half in the 20th minute.
Pushing in the line-out allowed Dominguez to put his side's first points on the board.
In the 34th minute, the faultless Dominguez made it 13-6 with his second penalty, awarded after a mazy 40-metre run by Francescato led to the Welsh forwards being caught off-side.
Wales hit back immediately, Thomas taking a pass from the blind-side of a scrum on the Italian 22 to brush off the hapless Ravazzolo's tackle and score in the same corner as James.

But penalties from Dominguez -- one almost from the halfway line -- gave warning of an Italian comeback and, in the 53rd minute, after another Jenkins penalty, winger Vaccari started a thrilling move in his own half that finished with Francescato racing in at the corner.
Dominguez's conversion and a 63rd minute penalty appeared to herald a famous Italian victory.
But, 22-21 down, Thomas led Wales' rearguard action, bursting through a shaky Italian defence to touch down under the posts for his side's third try, converted by Jenkins.
The Italians laid seige to the Welsh but first, Spannenberg, with his controversial decision, then Ravazzolo, who lost the ball with the line begging, denied them the vital try.
With Wales tiring, it was with some relief that Jenkins scored his fourth penalty of the match to clinch victory -- Wales' third over Italy in the past 12 months.

For Italy, eager to prove their credentials for the Five Nations, it was a disappointing prelude to matches in Ireland, Scotland and England as well as a visit from the Australians to Padua later this month.
Teams:

Italy: 15-Massimo Ravazzolo; 14-Paolo Vaccari (21-Javier Pertile 69th minute), 13-Stefano Bordon, 12-Ivan Francescato, 11-Leandro Manteri; 10-Diego Dominguez, 9-Alessandro Troncon; 8-Carlo Checchinato (18-Roberto Rampazzo 71st), 7-Orazio Arancio, 6-Andrea Sgorlon, 5-Diego Scaglia, 4-Pierpaolo Pedroni, 3-Franco Properzi Curti (17-Andrea Castellani 80th), 2-Carlo Orlandi, 1-Massimo Cuttitta (captain).

Wales: 15-Wayne Proctor (16-Leigh Davies 48th); 14-Simon Hill, 13-Gareth Thomas, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Dafydd James; 10-Neil Jenkins, 9-Robert Howley; 8-Stephen Williams, 7-Kingsley Jones (19-Martyn Williams 17th), 6-Hemi Taylor, 5-Derwyn Jones, 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-John Davies, 2-Jonathan Humphreys (captain), 1-Christian Loader.
